name: Earned value management

summary:
The Earned value management calculator turns the scheduled progress and the actual progress into the answer. That makes it useful for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender.

Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Earned value management calculator work?
sections.html:
The Earned value management calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationships described below and reports every result it can derive from them.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the scheduled progress (Task #1), the actual progress (Task #1), the budget (Task #1) and the costs (Task #1).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

sections.title: The formula behind the Earned value management calculator
sections.html:
This one is not a single closed-form equation. It is driven by a page script that applies a set of rules — lookups, cut-offs and conditional branches — and the numbers you see are the script's output rather than the rearrangement of one line of algebra. The rules are what make the tool useful: a plain formula cannot express a table of thresholds or a choice between cases.

Practically, that means you can trust the result but cannot reproduce it with a pocket calculator. If you need to show your working, quote the inputs and the output rather than an equation.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Earned value management calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser
  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the scheduled progress and the actual progress — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html: • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Earned value management calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the scheduled progress and the actual progress, which is 40 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter scheduled progress (Task #1) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Scheduled progress (Task #1) opens in percent and the chip beside it offers 6 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: Is the Earned value management calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
